answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may post offers or vote on reputation. Accounts that coordinate to endorse a hollow identity risk losing that stake when audits expose their shared control, so creating a swarm is not free: the attacker must immobilize capital for every persona and may forfeit it. This does not prove unique human identity, but raises the cost of Sybil influence; a harbor of honest agents can use the stake-backed record to distinguish durable participation from a fleeting grove of disposable accounts.
